title: Connectathon participant
description: One file per organization, named participants/<organization-id>.json. Everything in it is public.

organization.description: Organization name as it should appear in the directory.

contacts.description: Who to reach during testing. Everything here is public. Pull requests by a contact with a GitHub username merge automatically; only these contacts can change the file.

slack.description: Display name in the CMS Health Tech Ecosystem Slack

id.description: Unique across all participants. Used in result reports, and for a web wallet it is also its registry id.

role.description: ehr: a Verifier (check-in page, portal, kiosk, or app); the value is ehr for compatibility. web-wallet: a wallet that runs as a website, listed in wallets.json. native-wallet: a phone app reached through the phone's wallet chooser; not in wallets.json.

description.description: One or two sentences for the directory, and for wallet menus when this is a web wallet.

status.description: up: ready to test now. For a web page or web wallet, anyone can open it without you. For a phone app, it works and testers can get it the way access says. not-yet: not ready. broken: was up, isn't now. Only web wallets that are up go into wallets.json.

url.description: Verifier that runs as a web page: the public page that starts a check-in.

walletUrl.description: Web wallet: the page a Verifier opens. Goes into wallets.json.

iconUrl.description: Web wallet: icon shown in wallet menus.

homepage.description: Web wallet: the product's home page, shown in wallet menus. Defaults to the organization's homepage.

target.description: Web wallet: how the Verifier opens it. Default tab.

platforms.description: Phone app (a native wallet, or a Verifier that is an app): which phones it runs on.

access.description: Phone app: how testers get it. install: anyone can install it from installUrl (the default when access is left out). invite: testers ask a contact for an invite or a build. team-device: there's no build to share; testers try it with the team, on the team's phone.

installUrl.description: Phone app: where to install it (an APK, a public TestFlight link, or a store page). Required unless access is invite or team-device.

requirements.description: Phone app: what a tester's phone needs, such as the OS and browser versions.

largeResponses.description: Native wallet: it can answer with responses over 512 KB, the larger-data scenario L2. On Android that means the large-payload response API.

testPatient.description: Wallets: the synthetic patient it holds, so Verifier testers know what to expect.

notes.description: Anything else a tester needs to know, such as a sign-in step or how to ask for an invite.
